channel.title: Universal Design for Learning :: CS Two Year Refactor
channel.description: Working draft for faculty review. This page describes the general research basis for designing course materials with built-in flexibility rather than retrofitted accommodations. What Universal Design for Learning is Universal Design for Learning (UDL) applies an idea from architecture — design a building’s entrances and spaces to work for the widest range of bodies from the start, rather than building for one “standard” body and bolting on a wheelchair ramp later — to instructional design. CAST’s foundational articulation frames the target of instruction as the “expert learner,” and its central premise is that learner variability is the norm, not the exception: a course designed for one imagined average student will systematically underserve everyone who doesn’t match that profile, whereas a course built with multiple ways in from the outset serves a much wider range of learners without requiring an individual accommodation request for each one (Rose & Meyer, 2002). The current operational version of the framework is maintained and periodically revised by CAST (CAST, 2024).
